citation.authors: Gu Y, McNamara JA Jr, Sigler LM, Baccetti T
citation.title: Comparison of craniofacial characteristics of typical Chinese and Caucasian young adults

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 6 differences, all definitionMatch; every mean, SD and n agreed). All 38 values re-read from the page image of Table 1 (p. 206, PDF p. 2): agree. Decisions (merge notes): #31 facial axis a 'same', b 'close' → close (PTM vs Pt not stated), stored + 90 (owner 7 Oct); 'MP' #23 a 'same', b 'close' → close (plane not named); IMPA #57 a 'same', b 'close' → close (plane not named). Incisor mm rows and Wits close as both extractors. Selection: a 'ideal-aesthetic', b 'class-I-balanced' → class-I-balanced (normal occlusion and well-balanced faces, p. 206). Scale: a 'magnificationCorrected: true', b 'false' (both pre-date the scale field) → enlarged 8%, p. 206, by merge-notes ruling P27. No age band at first (no range printed; merge notes); a's computed sample.ageMean (19.9, not printed) dropped. Fix round 1 (2026-10-08, owner AGE-1 / MAL-1, rulings P42, P45, P47, review): ageBand [16, 30] on every row (owner AGE-1); Wits definitionNote drops '(owner 7 Oct)' - the owner's ruling was the Caucasian Wits. Wording (Task 9b-1, re-review minors): the age caveat says the ruling once; the band is described as about 1 SD below to 3 SD above the mean ages.

caveats: Beijing Chinese young adults from the Peking University orthodontic files, not originally from Guangdong or Fujian; untreated, normal occlusion, well-balanced faces judged by three Chinese orthodontists and three laypersons; cervical stage 6 (pp. 205-206). Men 19.3 ± 3.0 y (n 25), women 20.3 ± 3.4 y (n 40) (p. 205).

8% film enlargement: p. 206 says every cephalogram was standardised to 8 per cent magnification. Read as the mm values including an 8% enlargement (as McNamara 1984's 'enlargement factor included', whose samples and software the paper shares); stored as printed and converted to true size by the resolver (owner M-1, ruling P27).

No age range is printed (only mean ± SD by sex). Age band 16–30 on every row by owner ruling 8 Oct (AGE-1, age first): the paper gives mean ages 19.3 ± 3.0 (M) / 20.3 ± 3.4 (F), cervical stage 6; the band runs from about 1 SD below to 3 SD above the mean ages.

The paper does not define its mandibular plane ('MP', IMPA), occlusal plane (Wits), facial-axis points or incisor points; it cites Ricketts 1968 and McNamara 1984 and used Dentofacial Planner (p. 206). Those rows are close.
Head position during filming not stated. Lateral headfilms hand traced, landmarks verified by a second investigator, then digitised (p. 206).
Tables 3 to 6 (pp. 208-210) restate these values; Table 1, the group's own table, is used.
